subject: Token economics & latency: onboarding alignment and initial tuning plan
body:
From: Sara Pace <sara.pace@acmeinc.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Token economics & latency: kickoff request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Acme is ramping a new inference feature for on-device guidance and we want to get your team involved early on for cost/latency tuning during onboarding. Attached is a small workload_sample.json with a 48-hour traffic slice and a token-length histogram.

Top asks:
- Can Redwood help us pick quantization and batching configs that keep p95 under 200ms for the interactive flows?
- We need a sense of token-level cost delta for q4_0 vs q8_0 vs int8 runs.
- Recommend routing policies when we shift from prod pilot (low qps, high tail sensitivity) to steady-state (higher qps).

Ideal kickoff window: next Tue/Wed morning PST. Please let me know who from Redwood should attend — we’ll need both CS and an infra/ML engineer.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Pace | Head of Platform | Acme Robotics

Subject: Re: Token economics & latency: kickoff request

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the sample and the clear asks. Putting Marissa (CS lead) and Dylan (inference infra) on this thread so we can map a concise onboarding plan. I attached our standard redwood_onboarding_checklist.xlsx to show typical milestones.

Proposed 45-minute kickoff agenda:
- 5m introductions & goals
- 10m production traffic shape & SLOs (you)
- 10m baseline profiling approach (we)
- 10m quantization/profile candidates + perf/cost tradeoffs (Dylan)
- 10m rollout & routing policy options (Marissa + Rachel)

Pre-kickoff asks (helps us prepare):
- Confirm peak qps / avg qps and desired p50/p95 SLOs
- Provide expected max_context_length and a short list of longest prompts
- If you have any compliance/KM keys constraints note them now

Tentative kickoff slots (PST): Tue 2026-11-24 09:30, 10:30, 14:00. Which works?

Action: I’ll run a quick profile on the workload sample before the call and drop initial numbers.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Quick notes from infra POV before the call:
- For interactive p95 < 200ms we’ll likely target small micro-batches with aggressive async KV cache hits for stable prefixes.
- Quant candidates to test: q4_0 (best cost/quality starting point), q5_0 for a middle ground, and int8 only if validation shows negligible quality loss on your eval set.
- Rough batching targets: 8–32 tokens/batch depending on token length distribution. If your median request is 12 tokens, 16-token batches with prefix caching usually give best unit cost while preserving 95th percentile latency.
- Routing: start with single-region strict latency routing and a fallback to cheaper variant for non-interactive workloads. Use canary policy for model changes.

I attached a short perf sketch (initial_perf_estimate.pdf) with expected token-cost deltas at modest qps. I’ll run the sample through our profiler tomorrow and paste numbers.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
